p: Westwood Cross sits slap bang in the middle of the Isle of Thanet, between Margate, Broadstairs and Ramsgate, so you're never more than a few minutes from the sea. That's what makes it such a good base: bounce here when the weather's grim, and dash for the coast when the sun pops out.

Thanet has some wonderfully odd attractions. In Margate, the Shell Grotto is an underground passageway lined with millions of shells, and nobody knows for certain who built it or why. Kids love the mystery. In Ramsgate, the Ramsgate Tunnels take you into a network of old wartime air-raid shelters carved into the chalk cliffs, with guided tours telling the story of the people who sheltered there.

Over at Pegwell Bay, near Ramsgate, you'll find the Hugin, a replica Viking longship that commemorates the landing of the Saxons in this part of Kent. It's an impressive sight and a nice quick stop on a drive along the coast.

Broadstairs has strong links with Charles Dickens, who loved holidaying here, and the town celebrates him with a Dickens Festival. It's also home to Morelli's, a long-standing ice-cream parlour that has become something of an institution on the seafront.
Inland at Birchington, Quex Park houses the Powell-Cotton Museum, with its collections of natural history and objects from around the world.
All of Thanet is well served by buses, and the coastal towns are close enough that you can easily combine a few of these with a bouncy session in one busy day.
In the height of summer the coastal roads can be slow, so a bounce session at Westwood Cross is a handy way to dodge the busiest part of the day before heading for the beach.
